name: Paperman
tagline: Give your screen a softer, paper-like texture with an adjustable overlay.
description:
Paperman places a subtle paper-texture layer over the display to soften the hard uniformity of bright screens. Unlike a conventional blue-light filter, it is designed to change perceived texture and contrast while keeping color shifts small.

## Features

- Choose among nine paper-inspired textures as they become available in the current release.
- Adjust the strength of the overlay to suit the display and room lighting.
- Exclude color-sensitive or presentation applications from the effect.
- Schedule the texture around sunrise or custom hours.
- Use separate behavior for multiple monitors and pause on battery when desired.
- Snooze the effect temporarily or use a desktop-lamp mode for ambient light.

## Where it fits

Paperman is for readers, writers, and office workers who find a perfectly bright digital surface visually tiring. Designers and photographers should use exclusions whenever accurate color and contrast matter. The effect is subjective and is not a medical treatment or a substitute for appropriate display brightness, breaks, or clinical advice.

## Privacy and requirements

Paperman requires macOS 12 or later. The direct-download edition can keep the effect active in full-screen apps; App Store sandbox limits cause its overlay to switch off there. Screen-related permission may be necessary for the overlay and app exclusions.

## Pricing

Paperman costs $8.99 as a one-time purchase and is also available through Setapp.
